title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Act requires developers of AI‑powered physical systems—such as autonomous robots, drones, and smart manufacturing equipment—to coordinate with government regulators and industry partners to ensure safety, reliability, and compliance with established standards. It sets up a framework for data sharing, oversight, and liability safeguards so that these technologies can be deployed responsibly, protecting public welfare while encouraging innovation.

title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to provide further transparency and accountability for the use of content that is generated by artificial intelligence (generative AI) in political advertisements by requiring such advertisements to include a statement within the contents of the advertisements if generative AI was used to generate any image or video footage in the advertisements, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The policy would amend the 1971 Federal Election Campaign Act to make political ads more transparent about AI usage. It would require that any ad containing AI-generated images or videos must include a statement inside the ad disclosing the use of generative AI.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is legislation designed to safeguard democratic processes from misleading or manipulative AI-generated content. It establishes rules requiring transparency, accountability, and enforcement measures to ensure that AI tools cannot distort public opinion or interfere with fair elections.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act establishes guidelines and oversight mechanisms to ensure that AI systems capable of autonomous self‑improvement operate safely and transparently. It requires developers to implement monitoring protocols, report updates, and comply with regulatory standards to mitigate risks associated with rapidly evolving AI technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on constructing new data centers that run AI workloads, allowing time to evaluate their environmental and energy impacts. It gives regulators a set period to study the issue and develop guidelines or requirements for any future AI data center development.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The “Stop Rogue AI Act” proposes to curb the development and deployment of AI systems that pose significant safety or security risks. It aims to enforce stricter regulatory oversight and potentially halt the use of autonomous AI technologies that could act unpredictably or harmfully.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt on the construction and expansion of new AI data centers to address environmental and energy concerns. It aims to give lawmakers time to evaluate the long‑term impact of AI infrastructure on climate and energy consumption before allowing future growth.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a new federal board tasked with investigating cybersecurity incidents involving artificial intelligence. The board will oversee investigations, recommend safeguards, and help ensure AI systems meet national security and safety standards.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act is a legislative proposal aimed at ensuring that advances in artificial intelligence benefit the American public. It seeks to promote responsible AI development, protect privacy, and support American innovation and jobs through targeted funding and regulations.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act is a law that requires AI companies and developers in China to regularly submit detailed reports on their AI models, usage statistics, and potential societal impacts. This act aims to increase transparency, promote accountability, and help policymakers understand and regulate AI technology’s growth and influence across the country.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a law that limits the use of artificial intelligence in medical care, ensuring that human doctors remain the primary providers of diagnosis and treatment. It sets strict rules that AI tools can only support doctors, not replace them, to keep patient care personalized and accountable.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The bill proposes creating a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats inside the President’s Executive Office, dedicated to monitoring and addressing risks posed by AI and other advanced technologies. It also includes additional provisions to support related policy goals, although specific details are not provided in the title.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 aims to establish national standards for AI development, ensuring that new AI systems are safe, transparent, and ethically responsible. It requires researchers to meet rigorous testing and reporting requirements before deploying AI technologies that could impact public welfare.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 establishes comprehensive regulations for the development, deployment, and use of AI systems to protect public safety, privacy, and national security. It requires companies to conduct risk assessments, implement mitigation measures, disclose AI capabilities, and submit to oversight by a dedicated regulatory authority.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to address security challenges posed by AI technologies. The task force will develop standards, best practices, and guidelines to protect critical infrastructure, national security, and the public from AI‑related cyber threats.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution formally creates a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to oversee AI research, policy, and regulation. The committee will be tasked with reviewing AI developments, proposing guidelines, and ensuring responsible use of artificial intelligence.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 is designed to set up systematic ways to assess the safety and potential harms of AI systems. It likely outlines rules for risk assessment, reporting, and oversight by government bodies to reduce AI‑related risks.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a new set of laws designed to govern how artificial intelligence is developed, tested, and used in the United States. It aims to protect public safety, privacy, and fairness while encouraging innovation and accountability in AI technology.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes regulations to assess and mitigate the environmental footprint of AI technologies, including energy consumption, carbon emissions, and e‑waste. The act sets standards for transparency, accountability, and encourages sustainable AI development throughout the industry.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is designed to boost students’ understanding of artificial intelligence, teaching them how AI systems work and their societal impacts. It also establishes guidelines and resources for schools to responsibly incorporate AI tools into teaching while protecting student privacy and safety.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 is a proposed law that aims to make AI systems safer and more trustworthy by setting standards for how researchers develop and test new AI technologies. It also calls for oversight, transparency, and investment in safety measures so that AI can be used responsibly across society.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, working with the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to set up a pilot program that uses AI to strengthen cyber defenses for critical infrastructure. It also includes additional provisions for related actions.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to embed artificial‑intelligence education into school curricula, so that students learn how AI works, its benefits, and its risks from an early age. It also calls for teacher training, resource funding, and national standards to ensure that educators and schools are prepared to teach and guide students responsibly in an AI‑driven world.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act establishes guidelines and oversight for the use of artificial intelligence in processing veterans’ claims, aiming to ensure the technology operates fairly, transparently, and reliably. It requires that AI systems used in claims decisions be auditable, explainable, and subject to regular reviews to protect veterans’ rights and maintain trust in the benefits process.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 seeks to make sure that any artificial‑intelligence systems used by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs are clear and understandable to veterans and stakeholders. It requires companies and the VA to disclose how AI systems make decisions and to establish oversight so users can see how these tools affect services they receive.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act proposes a nationwide public awareness and education campaign to inform citizens about artificial intelligence, its benefits, risks, and responsible use. It aims to promote transparency, digital literacy, and empower individuals to make informed decisions about AI technologies.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate’s resolution stresses that protecting religious freedom and respecting authoritative texts are essential as artificial intelligence systems become more pervasive. It calls for policies that increase transparency and accountability in AI, ensuring these technologies align with diverse beliefs and values.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act establishes legal safeguards to prevent misleading or fraudulent uses of artificial intelligence, setting clear rules and penalties for deceptive AI practices. It aims to increase transparency and accountability in AI products and services so consumers can trust the information and interactions they encounter.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The directive instructs the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress about how artificial intelligence systems are used in handling information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. It covers AI’s role in acquiring, analyzing, querying, disseminating, or otherwise accessing that data.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to strengthen AI literacy and skills among students and workers by funding curriculum development, teacher training, and workforce programs. It aims to bridge the skills gap in AI‑related jobs, ensuring the U.S. workforce is prepared for the growing demand in AI technology sectors.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act is designed to promote the use and development of open‑source AI technologies, encouraging collaboration and innovation across the industry. The law seeks to increase transparency and accountability by ensuring that AI tools and models are accessible, well-documented, and governed by clear, public standards.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 seeks to prevent AI companies from using hidden or dynamic pricing tactics that inflate costs for consumers and to stop them from manipulating labor market wages to keep workers underpaid. It would require AI firms to disclose their pricing models and wage-setting practices, and impose penalties for non‑compliance.
